description: The session analysis script that creates sanitized session summaries, including timeout/error aggregation logic.
title: Session analyzer implementation

claim: The sanitized session report counted 2,035 entries, 107 subagent tool uses, 17 subagent tool errors, and 10 subagent-timeout indicators.
evidence: Report summary lists entries, tool counts, tool errors, and subagent_timeouts count.
relevance: Improvement should address repeated delegated-agent failures at orchestration and child-contract boundaries, not a single isolated timeout.
title: Session was subagent-heavy

claim: The longest timed turns in the sanitized report are subagent tool results, including approximately 600s, 566s, and two 300s child calls.
evidence: Longest Timed Turns table lists subagent durations of 600018ms, 565697ms, 300015ms, and 300010ms.
relevance: The proposal should add explicit timeout budgets, async/control handling, and stop rules for long-running child work.
title: Subagent turns hit timeout-scale durations

claim: The sanitized report recorded very large tool/text outputs, four compaction events, and an estimated cost above 55 cost units.
evidence: Largest Tool/Text Outputs includes outputs up to 166,878 characters; Compaction Events count is 4; cost_totals reports cost 55.37621.
relevance: Subagent handoffs should use compact receipts, file-only outputs, and context budgets to prevent parent/child drift and expensive transcript growth.
title: Session had context and output pressure

claim: The sanitized report counted 788 bash calls with 25 bash errors, 430 edit calls with 13 edit errors, and 122 JSONL validation/upsert calls.
evidence: Tool counts and Tool errors in the sanitized report list bash, edit, and cartographer_jsonl activity.
relevance: The workflow needs stronger child deliverables and deterministic receipts so the parent verifies rather than repeatedly finishing or repairing delegated work by hand.
title: Parent rework and tool-failure pressure was high

claim: The user reported that the parent needed to be told to use the auditor before calling the proposal complete.
evidence: Initial request explicitly identifies this as an observed issue in the authorized session.
relevance: Proposal/plan/implement workflows should make the Cartographer auditor gate mandatory or receipt-gated before completion when the auditor is available.
title: Auditor gate was missed in practice

claim: The user reported worker-agent issues where the parent had to finish the implementation.
evidence: Initial request explicitly identifies worker-agent handoff failures in the authorized session.
relevance: Pathfinder/worker contracts should require changed-file evidence, validation evidence, residual-risk reporting, and bounded self-review before a parent treats work as complete.
title: Worker handoffs left parent implementation burden

claim: pi-subagents guidance recommends structured acceptance for worker runs from plans/specs, separating task instructions from criteria, evidence, verify commands, stop rules, and bounded finalization turns.
evidence: pi-subagents skill section on validation contracts and structured acceptance describes criteria, evidence, verify, stopRules, and maxFinalizationTurns for worker handoffs.
relevance: Cartographer implement workflow can use runtime acceptance contracts rather than relying only on prose prompts.
title: Structured acceptance exists for worker handoffs

claim: pi-subagents guidance says an async implementation worker handoff is an intermediate state; the parent should follow with independent review, synthesis, fixes, and final validation unless worker-only output was explicitly requested.
evidence: pi-subagents review-loop and implementation guidance distinguish worker completion from reviewed completion.
relevance: Cartographer workflows should encode this distinction so parent finalization cannot skip auditor/reviewer gates after a worker reports done.
title: Worker completion is not final completion

claim: The implement skill names cartographer-pathfinder and cartographer-auditor as preferred agents, but several core procedure steps still dispatch or gate completion on the generic worker/reviewer roles.
evidence: Implement skill preferred-agent section references cartographer-pathfinder/auditor, while core rules and review steps describe worker/reviewer dispatch and approval.
relevance: The implementation workflow should be rewritten so Cartographer-specific agents are the default gates and builtin agents are explicit fallbacks.
title: Implement workflow has reviewer/auditor role mismatch

claim: The proposal and plan skills prefer cartographer-auditor in their agent-selection steps but their final validation sections still emphasize reviewer/oracle validation rather than an explicit auditor receipt when auditor is available.
evidence: Proposal skill lines around agent selection and final validation, plus plan skill lines around agent selection and final validation, show this inconsistency.
relevance: A mandatory deterministic-then-auditor completion gate would address the missed-auditor incident reported by the user.
title: Proposal and plan final validation under-specify auditor gate

claim: The session analyzer currently treats any record containing subagent/reviewer/worker and timeout-related strings as a subagent timeout, and the sanitized report's timeout table includes non-subagent tools with blank agents.
evidence: analyze_session.py timeout detection scans generic text fields, while the generated report lists read, bash, cartographer_index, and write rows in Subagent Timeouts.
relevance: Improving session analysis will make future subagent reliability evidence more precise and prevent misleading timeout counts.
title: Session timeout detection can overmatch

description: Prior accepted/drafted rationale for clean-context, receipt-first Cartographer workflow improvements, including timeout and context-bloat evidence.
title: workflow-optimization proposal

claim: The prior workflow-optimization proposal identified context bloat, large outputs, subagent timeout risk, and the need for optional, bounded Cartographer-specific subagents rather than generic clones.
evidence: workflow-optimization Problem Statement and Goals discuss large output/session cost, subagent timeout risk, deterministic checks before review, and specialized Cartographer agents.
relevance: This proposal should refine and enforce the existing direction for the specific subagent failures seen in the ADR session rather than reopening the whole workflow design.
title: Prior workflow optimization already chose clean-context subagent constraints

description: Prior rationale for trusted validation receipts, worker trust boundaries, and auditor-after-validation sequencing.
title: signed-receipts proposal

claim: The signed-receipts proposal states that workers/subagents propose changes while a trusted validation tool should produce hard validation evidence, with auditor review only after deterministic validation passes.
evidence: signed-receipts design describes worker/subagent proposals, trusted validation receipts, verify-topic, and auditor after validation.
relevance: Subagent reliability fixes should not rely on worker-authored receipts alone for completion gates.
title: Prior signed-receipts rationale separates worker output from trusted validation

description: Commit-safe aggregate analysis focused on tool-access, subagent outcome, acceptance, timeout, and custom-script signals from the authorized private session.
title: Sanitized subagent tooling analysis

claim: A focused sanitized tooling analysis found 107 subagent records but only 36 with explicit acceptance fields, 34 with explicit timeout/maxRuntime fields, and none with async or control fields.
evidence: Subagent tooling analysis summary lists subagent records and explicit acceptance/timeout/async/control field counts.
relevance: Reliability work should improve parent launch contracts and control settings, not only child prompts.
title: Subagent runs underused explicit runtime contracts

claim: The focused sanitized tooling analysis categorized signals for custom-script creation, Cartographer tool/CLI usage, edit failures, missing files, command-not-found errors, and tool schema/unavailable issues.
evidence: Tooling-Signal Categories table includes custom_script_created, cartographer_tools, exact_edit_failure, missing_file_or_dir, command_not_found, and tool_unavailable_or_unknown categories.
relevance: Dedicated read/validate helper tools could reduce ad-hoc shell scripts and repeated tool-use mistakes.
title: Tooling analysis shows shell and script friction

claim: Current Cartographer child agent definitions use basic file and shell tools rather than direct Cartographer index, JSONL, evidence, session, or ADR tools, so graph/artifact operations fall back to bash/CLI commands.
evidence: The tooling analysis findings and agent frontmatter show basic tool lists such as read/bash/write/edit without cartographer_index or cartographer_jsonl.
relevance: A least-privilege Cartographer artifact tool for child agents would improve speed and reliability without granting broad mutation permissions.
title: Child agents lack direct Cartographer tool access
